title: Nuclear spin in a magnetic field
caption: A ¹H nucleus has two spin states that have the same energy until a magnetic field is applied. In a field they split: aligned with the field (α) is lower, against it (β) higher. Radio waves of exactly the gap flip spins; the gap depends on the local field, which is what chemical shift measures.
alt: Energy diagram: one level with no field, splitting into a lower α level and a higher β level in a field, with a radio-frequency arrow between them.
description: No field: one energy for both spin states.
In field B₀: α (aligned) lower, β (opposed) higher.
Absorbing radio waves of energy ΔE flips α to β.

claims.name: the aligned (α) state is lower in energy
